questions.stem: What is one option a firm has when a competitor reduces their price?
questions.explanation: Lowering their own prices is a common response to remain competitive. Ignoring the competitor may lead to losing market share.

distractorRationale.b: Ignoring the competitor could result in losing customers to them.
distractorRationale.c: Increasing prices would likely drive customers away, especially if competitors are cheaper.
distractorRationale.d: Stopping production is not a viable response to price changes.

questions.stem: Why might a firm choose to hold its prices steady when costs rise?
questions.explanation: Holding prices steady can help maintain customer loyalty, as customers may appreciate price stability. Increasing profit margins is unlikely if prices are held steady.

distractorRationale.b: Holding prices steady does not increase profit margins; it may decrease them.
distractorRationale.c: Attracting new customers typically requires competitive pricing, not price stability.
distractorRationale.d: Holding prices does not directly reduce production costs.

questions.stem: What is a potential risk of engaging in a price war?
questions.explanation: A price war can lead to lower profit margins as firms continuously cut prices. Increased market share is not guaranteed and can be detrimental in the long run.

distractorRationale.a: Increased market share is not a guaranteed outcome of a price war; it can lead to losses instead.
distractorRationale.c: Customer loyalty may decrease if prices fluctuate too much.
distractorRationale.d: A price war typically harms brand reputation rather than enhancing it.

questions.stem: Holding prices steady during rising costs is always beneficial for a firm.
questions.explanation: While holding prices steady can maintain customer loyalty, it may not always be beneficial as it can lead to reduced profits if costs continue to rise.
